This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and baked data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**Answer.**
2017 East 17th Street, Brooklyn is outside the modeled flooding in the NYC DEP stormwater scenarios for 2050 SLR (2.13 in/hr) and 2080 SLR (3.66 in/hr), as well as the current SLR scenario [dep_moderate_2050][dep_extreme_2080][dep_moderate_current].

**Hazard Reader.**
This address sits outside the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM) [sandy_inundation]. This address sits in FEMA flood zone X, per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970352F, effective 2007 [fema_nfhl]. No Hurricane Ida (Sept 2021) high-water marks were surveyed within 800 m of this address. Nearest USGS-surveyed mark: Coney Island Ave., between Ave. P and Ave. O, Midwood, Brooklyn (1351 m away) [ida_hwm].

**Live Observer.**
No FloodNet sensors deployed within 600 m of this address [floodnet]. 34 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years. Most common descriptor: Catch Basin Clogged/Flooding (Use Comments) (SC) [nyc311].

**Out of scope.** This briefing does not assess title, structural condition, or compliance with specific zoning rules. Where a probe was offline at run time, the relevant section omits that signal.
